additional_findings: Project Zero (browser-streamed viewer) is being discontinued: Modem World, 22 Apr 2026, 'Linden Lab announces Project Zero to end'. The brief's 2025 MAU rebound attributes half of new users to Project Zero; that funnel has since been removed, and the brief's design implication about streamed access as a first-class tier needs this caveat.

Acquisition vs retention: at the Sept 2025 LL Zoom call the Lab said mobile + Project Zero reach ~10x the trial volume, but only ~7% of incoming users are retained (Modem World). Low-barrier clients solved acquisition, not retention; a successor must design for 30/90-day retention, not trial counts.
DAU declined while MAU rose: Oberwager (NWN, Nov 2024): 'our DAU has gone down, that's very concerning'. Publish DAU/MAU ratio, not MAU alone.

MAU definitions unreconciled: Daniel Voyager (May 2026) estimates 1.15M-1.45M unique 30-day logins vs the company's 600-620K MAU; no public definition of 'active'. A successor should define active-user metrics (session threshold, bots excluded) from day one.

Concurrency 2020-2026: pandemic peak 60,068 (20 Apr 2020), 53,016 (19 Feb 2024), 49,798 (24 Mar 2025), 48,802 (1 Apr 2026 YTD). Concurrency drifts down while reported MAU rises, consistent with lighter mobile/streamed sessions.

Region content budgets have been frozen since November 2016 (Mainland Full 22,500 LI; private Full 20,000 / 30,000 paid; Homestead 5,000; Openspace 1,000). A decade without a capacity-tier change is itself evidence of the fixed-unit lock-in.

Sansar sale structure: Linden Lab kept Tilia (the regulated payments/money-transmission layer) and shed the world; Wookey contracts Tilia for Sansar tokens. The compliance/payments layer is the durable asset; a successor should build it as a separable component.
MFA was made mandatory on all Second Life web properties (including Project Zero) in March 2025, indicating how late basic account-security modernisation arrived.
